choices.misconception: I collected the x terms on the wrong side and changed the sign of the 7.
I subtracted 5 from both sides and then divided by 1 with the wrong sign.
I read the 5 on the right as the answer without solving anything.
I added 7 and 12 together at the end rather than stopping at 12.

hints: Gather the x terms on one side.
Subtract 2x from both sides to leave a single x term, then move the constant across. Substituting your answer back into both sides is a free check that costs seconds.

solutions.reliable: Subtracting 2x from both sides gives x - 7 = 5, so x = 12. Checking, 3 x 12 - 7 = 29 and 2 x 12 + 5 = 29, which agree. The transferable idea: substituting the answer back into the original equation is the cheapest check available, and on a multiple-choice paper you can test the choices directly.
solutions.elegant: Testing the five choices is faster than rearranging, and only one makes both sides agree.

whyOnTest: Back-solving from the choices is a core contest habit, and the sign-slip answers are the ones on offer.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
